p01.why: Casts in both directions between a scoped enumeration and int are valid, and both assertions hold; there is no main, so the program is not run.

p02.why: 300 does not fit in unsigned char, so the enumerator value narrows.

p03.why: Each early declaration has a known underlying type, the later definitions agree with them, and F can be value-initialized with empty braces.

p04.why: A scoped value is compared with an integer.

p05.why: Inside its own value the name value still means the outer constant 12, so the enumerator is 12 and get returns 12.

p06.why: The two declarations of F give different underlying types.

p07.why: A scoped enumeration without a type has underlying type int.

p08.why: Each integer first converts to the fixed underlying type: 300 to 44, 200 to -56, -1 to 255, and 5 to true, so all assertions hold.

p09.why: Red belongs to a scoped enumeration and is named without Color::.

p10.why: Two values of the same scoped enumeration can be compared.

p11.why: Inside the list of an enumeration without a fixed type, letter has the type of its initializer, char, so check is 1.

p12.why: A scoped value is used in arithmetic.

p13.why: The values follow the sequence rule and the assertion holds.

p14.why: E has no fixed underlying type, so it cannot be initialized from an integer in braces.

p15.why: An unscoped enumeration declared without enumerators must give its underlying type.

p16.why: Unscoped values promote to int, so the initialization and arithmetic are valid.

p17.why: No standard integer type holds both 2^63 and -1; GCC accepts with a 128-bit type, while Clang and EDG reject.

p18.why: b is a plus one, 6, and d is c plus one, 2.

p19.why: Color holds 0 to 3, so converting 5 is undefined; the specification does not say whether the undefined-behavior sanitizer stops this conversion, and my guess is that its enum check stops the run at the load.

p20.why: A scoped value cannot be a condition.

p21.why: n is not a constant expression.

p22.why: ++ is applied to an enumeration with no user-declared operator.

p23.why: B gets 2147483648, the enumeration has no fixed type, so the implementation picks a wider underlying type that holds it.

p24.why: Inside the lists, a has type int, f1 has type long, and p1 has type unsigned; after the list p1 has type Plain.

p25.why: The enumerator Red is already declared in the enclosing scope as a variable.

p26.why: An explicit cast of a scoped value to bool is valid.

p27.why: The values fit their fixed underlying types, and the sizes follow those types.

p28.why: Two enumerators can have the same value.

p29.why: The scoped enumeration has underlying type int, and 2^40 does not fit.

p30.why: The underlying type is implementation-defined, and the evidence says the compilers use the size of int by default.

p31.why: 300 narrows when it converts to unsigned char.

p32.why: Both enumerations have fixed underlying types that hold 200 and 1000, so the casts are valid in constant evaluation.

p33.why: A scoped value cannot be an operand of !.

p34.why: Inside the list A has type int, so A * 2 is 8.

p35.why: using enum can name an alias of an enumeration.

p36.why: Both unscoped values promote to int; the specification says nothing about mixing two enumeration types, so I assume it is valid.

p37.why: C has only an opaque declaration, so it is not complete at using enum.

p38.why: An integer does not convert implicitly to an unscoped enumeration.

p39.why: Two enumerators have the same name.

p40.why: Unscoped enumerators can be named with or without the enumeration.

p41.why: Initialization with = and a braced integer is not valid.

p42.why: using enum brings Red and Green into the global scope.

p43.why: E is distinct from int and from F, A has type E, and +A has type int.

p44.why: Big needs a 64-bit underlying type, and Neg can hold -1.

p45.why: The declarations disagree on scoped versus unscoped.

p46.why: An empty enumeration without a fixed type holds 0 and 1.

p47.why: An initializer of enumeration type gives that type, so copy has type Old inside the list.

p48.why: The implicit value 2^31 does not fit in the fixed type int.

p49.why: 8 is outside 0 to 7; Clang rejects the cast in constant evaluation, while GCC and EDG accept it.

p50.why: count has the type of its initializer, short, without promotion; I assume the const of small is dropped.

p51.why: second needs a type wider than int; which one is unspecified, but every candidate makes kind nonzero.

p52.why: An int is initialized from a scoped value.

p54.why: bool is a valid underlying type, and const on the underlying type is ignored.

p55.why: A using declaration can name one enumerator of a scoped enumeration.

p56.why: Red is already declared in the global scope.

p57.why: Values 1 and 4 need 3 bits, so 7 is in range.

p58.why: Both enumerations have fixed underlying types, so direct initialization from a braced integer is valid.

p59.why: double is not an integer type.
